D010-D006_h001.question:
"Honestly, it's been a tough year. The last couple of months, I was on top of the world. My content was getting so much traction, I was brimming with ideas, and I just couldn't sit still – always buzzing, you know? My mind was racing, and I found myself talking non-stop, sometimes for hours, about all these big plans. I even sank a significant chunk of my savings into this 'sure-thing' crypto venture that, looking back, was probably a bit impulsive. My drive was through the roof, and I was seeing men everywhere, feeling this intense urge that was pretty new for me. But then things started getting weird. I began seeing shadows, glimpses of figures, especially at night, and I felt this sickening conviction that my casual boyfriend was cheating on me, even though there was no real proof.

Before all that, for about five months, it was the opposite. I couldn't drag myself out of bed. Everything felt heavy, grey. I lost all interest in pretty much everything – my work, hobbies, even just grabbing a coffee with friends felt like a monumental effort. I just felt this deep, unending sadness, and making even the smallest decision, like what to wear, would completely paralyze me."

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h001.answer: A & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h002.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been quite a rollercoaster for the past few months. Roughly two months ago, I had this surge of energy. I couldn't sit still, felt like I had to be constantly moving, talking to everyone. My husband would tell you I was far more sociable, always calling up old friends, even trying to get involved in some online business ventures – probably not the wisest, looking back. I just felt… electric, but it often tipped into irritability. The smallest thing would set me off, which isn't like me.

Then, for about five months now, it’s like a thick fog has rolled in. I just feel so down, like a heavy blanket over everything. I don't want to talk to anyone, not even my husband sometimes. My head feels so cloudy, like I can't quite grasp things. And the strangest part, it's hard to explain, but I sometimes get this metallic taste in my mouth, even if I haven't eaten anything. And I've been so worried about my insides, convinced something is dreadfully wrong with my organs, even after checks come back clear. It’s been tough to keep up with my census work, let alone anything else."

    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

But sticking to one thing was impossible; I’d jump from a script idea to researching ancient history to calling up friends in the middle of the night. I had so much energy I couldn't sit still for a second, and honestly, the smallest things would just set me off, making me snap at people. Around that time, things also started getting really weird. I kept seeing things out of the corner of my eye – shadowy figures mostly – and I became absolutely convinced my ex was talking to all my colleagues, trying to sabotage my career and ruin my reputation with baseless rumors. It’s been tough, really impacting my ability to do anything properly.

And sometimes it feels like my professors, or even people on the street, are sending me coded messages through their gestures or what they say on TV. It’s like they know something about me, and they're hinting at it. It's all just so overwhelming, and I can't seem to get anything real done.
